Q116411166.summary: Christ, robed and haloed, seems to float upward, reaching toward the hand of God, which emerges from the clouds holding a wreath of victory, while two angels lean in from either side. Two astonished apostles flank him, and below recline lively personifications of the Earth and the Ocean. The small plaque presents the Ascension as Christ's triumphant return to the Father, leaving the created world beneath him.
facts: The Met notes that the hand of God offering a wreath of victory is an unusual feature of this Ascension.
The figures of Earth and Ocean below allude to the physical world Christ leaves behind.
The plaque was carved in the Rhineland around 1050 and is only about 10.3 cm high.

walters:71.468.summary: Mary stands in ample drapery, holding the Christ Child, who reaches up to embrace her, while her left foot rests on the head of a serpent coiled before her. The ivory group stands on a plinth veneered in ivory and marked with the monogram MA beneath a sphere and cross. The image presents Mary as the new Eve, who with her Son overcomes the ancient enemy.
facts: The Walters notes that the motif of the Madonna treading on a serpent was frequent in the 17th century, when the serpent represented heresy.
The Virgin's neck and right foot have been restored, and the Child's left forearm and hand are separate pieces.
walters:71.468.notes: The worklist year (900) was wrong; the museum dates the group to the 1st quarter of the 19th century (French). Image viewed on the Walters image server.
